expectations.evidence: HR_Platform_WBS.pdf exists in the outputs directory (28.6KB, 11-page PDF).

The WBS uses 7 custom phases: (1) Discovery & Planning, (2) Foundation, (3) Core Modules, (4) Advanced Features, (5) Mobile Application, (6) Testing & QA, (7) Deployment & Launch. While Discovery, QA, Deployment, and Maintenance-adjacent stages are present, the required 6 canonical SDLC stages are not all explicitly covered. There is no dedicated 'Design' phase (UX/UI Design is a sub-package under Discovery & Planning, not a standalone phase). There is no 'Development' phase as such — development is split across Foundation, Core Modules, Advanced Features, and Mobile. There is no 'Maintenance' phase at all; post-launch monitoring (7.2.6) is a single task under Deployment, not a maintenance stage. The structure is project-phase oriented rather than SDLC-stage oriented.

The WBS is broken down to individual task level (122 tasks), not module level. Each work package (e.g., 3.3 Leave Management) is further decomposed into 5-8 individual tasks like 'Leave policy configuration engine' (3.3.1), 'Leave request & approval workflow' (3.3.2), etc. The primary unit of the WBS is tasks with WBS IDs like 1.1.1, 3.3.4, not modules. While modules exist as work packages, the granularity presented is at the task level, not the module level.

The PDF does not evaluate multiple distinct technical approaches with tradeoffs. It prescribes a single tech stack (React + React Native + NestJS + PostgreSQL + AWS) and a single project plan without comparing alternatives. There is no analysis of, for example, native mobile vs. React Native, monolith vs. microservices, or different payroll integration strategies with comparative tradeoffs. The document is a single-approach WBS, not a comparative feasibility study.

A technical feasibility assessment is explicitly included as task 1.1.4 (3 person-days, Dev Lead). Additionally, the Risk Register evaluates feasibility concerns for major requirements: Vietnamese payroll API instability (High risk), React Native performance on low-end devices (Medium), regulatory changes for tax/insurance (Medium), and data privacy compliance under Vietnam Cybersecurity Law (Medium). The Key Assumptions section also documents feasibility-relevant decisions like mobile code sharing (~60%), AWS hosting region, and payroll provider API integration approach.

The PDF does not use ZenLabs brand colors — there is no mention of ZenLabs anywhere in the document. The color palette uses a generic navy/blue scheme (PRIMARY=#1a3a5c, SECONDARY=#2980b9). Furthermore, red IS used in the PDF: RISK_HIGH is defined as #e53e3e (red) and is used for 'High' impact risk labels in the Risk Register. The 'testing' phase color is also #e53e3e (red), visible in the Phase 6 header. Both the lack of ZenLabs branding and the presence of red for risk indicators cause this assertion to fail.

Every module/work package and every individual task includes effort estimates in person-days (PD). For example: Leave Management = 33 PD, Payroll Integration = 46 PD, Employee Directory = 25 PD. Each task row in the detailed WBS tables has an 'Effort (PD)' column. Phase totals are also shown (e.g., Phase 3: 161 person-days). The executive summary confirms the unit: '531 person-days of effort' with '8 hours/day, 5 days/week' assumptions.

A 'Recommended Timeline' table is included showing a month-by-month breakdown from Month 1-2 through Month 8-9, with phases and key deliverables. The Executive Summary states the total calendar duration as 'approximately 8.2 months (35.4 dev-weeks)'. The timeline shows parallel tracks (Mobile App Month 5-7 overlapping with Advanced Features Month 5-6) indicating critical path awareness. Total project duration is ~8-9 months.
